findings.description: SATISFIED. Both cases are asserted and both discriminate. Planted lint defect (suite 1080-1093): my own run against a scope with a bogus_key planted after the migration commit printed 'FAIL <scope>: verify-lint: FAIL <file>: frontmatter-known-keys: `bogus_key` is in neither key order' plus 'lint failures: 1' and exited 1. Abort case (suite 1004-1026) runs verify-migration.sh out of a copied scripts/ whose lint-scope.sh is a stub echoing one stderr line and exiting 2; verification exits nonzero, reports 'lint failures: unknown (aborted before a summary)', and names the exit status. I proved the abort case really is the discriminator by mutation: a grep-based mutant (reads the 'failures:' summary, ignores exit status) and a repo-relative-path mutant (lint_bin=inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh) each fail the suite at exactly that assertion. Script reads the status at verify-migration.sh:98-121 and resolves the sibling at :96 via dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}". RULING on the yq preflight: the worker's reading is correct and the clause is satisfied without a suite assertion. The task's check_method switches subject mid-sentence -- 'confirm both cases are asserted' (the suite) then 'Confirm the script reads the lint's exit status, resolves the lint as a sibling ..., and carries its own yq preflight' (the script). Constitution C-6 names exactly two suite cases and lists removing yq from PATH among 'two triggers that look like they would work and don't', i.e. a trap for the checker, not an assertion the suite must carry. Confirmed by source read and by execution.
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/scripts/verify-migration.sh:96-121; tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:1004-1026,1080-1093. Mutation runs: grep-based lint mutant -> suite exit=1, last line 'verify-migration.sh exited zero against an aborting lint'; repo-relative lint_bin mutant -> suite exit=1, same line. Direct run of the shipped script on a stub-lint copy: 'FAIL <scope>: verify-lint: lint-scope.sh aborted with exit status 2 before printing a summary'. yq preflight executed directly with a PATH lacking yq: exit=2, stderr 'yq is required and not on PATH (brew install yq)' (verify-migration.sh:70-73, byte-identical to lint-scope.sh:63-66).

findings.description: FAILS the 'counts targets from the pre-migration ref rather than the post-migration tree' half of the check. The script itself is correct (verify-migration.sh:129-137 enumerates via git ls-tree/git show at $since_ref), but NO suite assertion pins it, so the clause's own failing example is untested. Proof by mutation: I replaced since_tree_targets' body with a post-migration-tree read (find "$scope" -name '*.md' -exec cat {} + | grep -oE '\[\[[^]|]*' ...) in a copy of the repo and the whole suite still exited 0. Both link scenarios are blind to the difference: in the passing scope the link lives in note A, which survives migration, and in the combo scope the DELETED file is the link's target (note B), not its source -- note A is still in the tree carrying the link either way. Fix: give the suite a scope where the link is only observable at the --since ref, e.g. commit the deletion of the note that CONTAINS a wiki link (or drop the link line in the post-migration commit) and assert both the 'links checked: N' count and the verify-link failure; a tree-based sweep then reports 'links checked: 0' and passes, while the shipped implementation fails. The other two halves of the check are satisfied: id-fallback count asserted at 978 ('links checked: 1 (id fallback: 1)', which I reproduced), verify-link failure asserted at 1060 (reproduced).
findings.evidence: inbox-to-memory/scripts/verify-migration.sh:129-147 vs tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:978,1060. Mutation run (tree-reading since_tree_targets, repo copied to scratch): 'MUTANT-A (tree-based links) suite exit=0 / inbox-to-memory smoke: ok'. Contrast: the porcelain mutant for C-8 exits 1 on the same suite, so the harness does catch implementation swaps it actually asserts.

findings.description: SATISFIED. The script reads git diff --name-status -M "$since_ref" (verify-migration.sh:176-191) and never git status --porcelain. The suite's combo scope commits both a git mv and a git rm after the migration commit and asserts the tree is porcelain-clean first (1046-1049), then requires separate verify-rename lines for the rename and the deletion (1061-1062) and 'failures: 3' (1063). I rebuilt that scenario by hand: porcelain printed nothing, git diff --name-status -M printed 'R084 ... one-vendor-per-region-G2k65qG3Nc.md -> ...-renamed-...md' and 'D notes/...-P5spzLt4Bz.md', and the shipped script exited 1 naming the rename and the deletion on separate lines. Mutation confirms the assertion discriminates: swapping the diff for a porcelain read makes the suite exit 1 with 'renames: 0 / deletions: 0 / failures: 1'.

My run: 'porcelain: []' then 'R084	_memory/decisions/one-vendor-per-region-G2k65qG3Nc.md	..._renamed_...' and 'D	notes/2025-11-18-atlas-working-session-P5spzLt4Bz.md'; verify exit=1 with 'verify-rename: `...G2k65qG3Nc.md` renamed to `...renamed-G2k65qG3Nc.md`' and 'verify-rename: `notes/2025-11-18-atlas-working-session-P5spzLt4Bz.md` deleted'. Porcelain mutant: suite exit=1.

findings.description: SATISFIED. Byte-identity is asserted across two failing runs by hashing the whole scope before and after (suite 1053-1058 combo, 1089-1092 lint defect, via hash_scope() at 947-949 -- find -type f -exec shasum, .git excluded). I re-derived it rather than reading intent: on my own committed-rename/deletion scope the before and after shasum listings were identical while the run exited 1. Multiple defects in one run are reported, not just the first: that same run printed three FAIL lines from two different sweeps (verify-link, verify-rename rename, verify-rename deletion) and 'failures: 3'. The script has no write path -- nothing in verify-migration.sh redirects into the scope, and the record is a printf to stdout only.
findings.evidence: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:947-949,1053-1063,1089-1092. My run against a hand-built scope: BEFORE/AFTER shasum listings compared -> 'BYTE-IDENTICAL: yes' with exit=1 and 'failures: 3', all three FAIL lines present in one run's output.

findings.description: FAILS one of three required assertions: the suite never pins the record paragraph to that run's real counts. Suite 982-983 asserts only the prefix 'Verified $v_pass against $v_pass_since' and the trailing 'Paste this paragraph into the scope's patterns journal.'; the counts asserted at 977-981 come from the summary block (which prints on failing runs too), not from the paragraph. Proof by mutation: hard-coding the paragraph's counts to '0 lint failures, 0 links checked (0 by id fallback), 0 renames, 0 deletions' while the run really checked 1 link with 1 id fallback leaves the suite at exit 0 -- exactly the shape of the clause's failing example, a record certifying numbers the run didn't produce. Fix: add one assertion on the paragraph's interior, e.g. require_output "$pass_out" "0 lint failures, 1 links checked (1 by id fallback), 0 renames, 0 deletions". The other two halves ARE satisfied and I reproduced both: no file under the scope contains the paragraph after a passing run (suite 987-994, and my own grep -rlF over the scope returned nothing, with the patterns-journal/ sentinel intact), and a failing run emits no record (suite 1064-1068; my combo run's output ends at 'failures: 3' with no 'Verified ... against' line).
findings.evidence: tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:977-994,1064-1068; inbox-to-memory/scripts/verify-migration.sh:204-207. Mutation run (paragraph counts hard-coded to zeros): 'MUTANT-F (hardcoded record counts) suite exit=0 / inbox-to-memory smoke: ok'. My passing run printed 'links checked: 1 (id fallback: 1)' and a paragraph reading '... 0 lint failures, 1 links checked (1 by id fallback), 0 renames, 0 deletions', so the implementation is right and only the assertion is missing.

findings.description: SATISFIED. git diff 1f17478 -- tests/ removes exactly one line and it is not an assertion: the old one-line Raw Content placeholder in the old-only fixture note, replaced by the C-1/C-2 seam the constitution's 'testability fixture' section mandates. Rather than eyeballing the diff I extracted every require_*/refute_* line from tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh at 1f17478 and from the working copy, sorted both, and diffed the sets: nothing from the base is missing, so no line was deleted, reworded, or loosened. Counts went 152 -> 187 require_* and 12 -> 17 refute_*. All three suites exit 0.

findings.description: SATISFIED. Ran the constitution's C-13 command verbatim: exit 0. Printing the same pathspec pair without the test -z wrapper confirms the emptiness is real rather than a swallowed error -- no tracked diff and no untracked file outside inbox-to-memory/, tests/, .agent-guild/, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore. The task's two artifacts sit inside the allowed prefixes, and git status shows nothing under SKILL.md or references/.

findings.description: SATISFIED. The header (verify-migration.sh:2-7) states the constraint that shapes the script -- git history over working-tree status, because by the time anyone runs this the apply is committed and git status reads clean -- which is the same why-first register as lint-scope.sh:2-12 and migrate-scope.sh:2-14. Every section comment carries a reason a reader couldn't get from the code: :68-69 on owning the yq refusal so a sibling doesn't take the blame, :92-95 on sibling resolution being the seam the abort case is tested through, :104-108 on why the exit status is read instead of the summary, :124-128 on reading targets at the ref, :142 on template placeholders not being links, :170-173 on porcelain reporting clean for the committed case. No comment restates the next line, no rule-of-three padding, no bolded inline headers, no promotional framing. Failure strings match the neighbors' 'FAIL <file>: <diagnostic>: <detail>' shape (lint-scope.sh:75). One cosmetic wart, below the bar for a finding: wrapping a lint FAIL line inside verification's own fail() doubles the word, e.g. 'FAIL <scope>: verify-lint: FAIL <file>: frontmatter-known-keys: ...'. The record paragraph's final prose belongs to T-004 per the task file and was not judged here.
